question: A class of organic compounds that contain an oxygen between two alkyl groups is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is ether.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An ether is an organic compound in which an oxygen atom is bonded to two alkyl (or aryl) groups, represented generally as R–O–R'. (ईथर — ऑक्सीजन द्वारा जुड़े दो एल्किल समूह)

 

• Ethers are formed by the dehydration of alcohols (e.g., two molecules of ethanol give diethyl ether, C₂H₅–O–C₂H₅, in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid at 413 K).

 

• Ethers are relatively unreactive and are widely used as solvents in organic reactions; diethyl ether was historically used as an anaesthetic.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Alcohols (R–OH) contain a hydroxyl group attached to a carbon; aldehydes (R–CHO) and ketones (R–CO–R') contain a carbonyl group (C=O), with aldehydes having at least one hydrogen attached to the carbonyl carbon and ketones having two carbon substituents.

 

NOTE

 

• Alcohol (Option 1): Contains an –OH (hydroxyl) group attached to a carbon atom, not an oxygen bridging two alkyl groups.

 

• Aldehyde (Option 2): Contains a carbonyl group (–CHO) at the end of a carbon chain.

 

• Ketone (Option 3): Contains a carbonyl group (C=O) flanked by two carbon groups, not an oxygen directly bonded to two separate alkyl groups.

question: The 'Donate-a-Pension' campaign under______ scheme, was launched in the 'Iconic Week' celebrations by the Labour Ministry from 7 to 13 March 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Donate-a-Pension' initiative was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment on 7 March 2022 under the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM) scheme, as part of the government's 'Iconic Week' celebrations (7–13 March 2022). (दान-ए-पेंशन — प्रधानमंत्री श्रम योगी मानधन योजना)

 

• Under the initiative, any citizen (a 'Pradhan', i.e. donor) can sponsor/donate the contribution of an unorganised sector worker towards their PM-SYM pension account.

 

• PM-SYM itself is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme for unorganised sector workers (aged 18-40 years, monthly income up to ₹15,000), guaranteeing a minimum monthly pension of ₹3,000 after the age of 60.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• PM-SYM is administered through the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) as the pension fund manager and implemented via Common Service Centres (CSCs).

 

NOTE

 

• Pradhan Mantri HRIDAY (Option 1): Heritage City Development and Augmentation Yojana, launched in 2015 for preservation of heritage cities.

 

• Pradhan Mantri eDonate (Option 3): Not an actual government scheme; a distractor option.

 

• Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (Option 4): An irrigation scheme launched in 2015 to expand cultivated area with assured irrigation.

question: Under whose reign was the maximum number of books in Persian on classical Indian Music written?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aurangzeb.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Despite his personal reputation for austerity, the largest number of Persian-language treatises on Hindustani classical music were compiled during the reign of Aurangzeb (1658-1707). (औरंगजेब — फारसी संगीत ग्रंथ सर्वाधिक)

 

• The most notable of these is 'Rag Darpan' by Faqirullah (also called Saif Khan), written in 1666, a major Persian treatise on Hindustani music theory and the musicians of the period.

 

• Other Persian musicological works of this era include the 'Shams-ul-Aswat'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ironically, Aurangzeb is often remembered for having banned music at his court in his later years, yet the volume of Persian musicological literature peaked precisely during his reign, largely authored by nobles and scholars in his administration.

 

NOTE

 

• Shah Jahan (Option 1): Known chiefly as a patron of architecture (Taj Mahal, Red Fort), not for the largest body of Persian music literature.

 

• Jahangir (Option 2): Remembered more for patronage of painting and his memoir Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri.

 

• Akbar (Option 3): His court housed the musician Tansen, but the peak output of Persian music treatises came later, under Aurangzeb.

question: When was the first Session of the Lok Sabha of independent India held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 13th May 1952.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Following India's first general elections (held between October 1951 and February 1952), the first Lok Sabha was constituted, and its first session began on 13 May 1952. (प्रथम लोकसभा सत्र — 13 मई 1952)

 

• President Dr. Rajendra Prasad addressed the joint session of both Houses of Parliament for the first time after the general elections.

 

• G.V. Mavalankar was elected as the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Before this, a provisional Parliament (the Constituent Assembly acting as interim legislature) had functioned from 26 January 1950 to April 1952.

 

NOTE

 

• 13th June 1951, 13th June 1952 (Options 1 & 2): Incorrect dates/months; they do not correspond to the first Lok Sabha session.

 

• 13th May 1951 (Option 4): Incorrect year — the general elections were not yet complete in May 1951.

question: The Cabinet Mission came to India in ________ to discuss the ultimate transfer of power.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1946.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Cabinet Mission, comprising three British Cabinet ministers — Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps, and A.V. Alexander — arrived in India in March 1946 to discuss and plan the transfer of power from British to Indian hands. (कैबिनेट मिशन — 1946)

 

• It proposed a three-tier federal structure for India and rejected the demand for a full, separate Pakistan, instead suggesting grouping of provinces.

 

• It also led to the formation of the Constituent Assembly of India and an interim government.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Following differences over the plan's implementation, the Muslim League observed 'Direct Action Day' on 16 August 1946.

 

NOTE

 

• 1945 (Option 2): The Wavell Plan and the Shimla Conference took place in 1945, not the Cabinet Mission.

 

• 1943 (Option 3): This year saw the Bengal Famine, not the Cabinet Mission.

 

• 1942 (Option 4): The Cripps Mission came to India in 1942, and the Quit India Movement was launched the same year.

question: The 'Kambala' festival is organised by farming communities in the state of __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kambala is a traditional buffalo race held in muddy paddy fields, organised by farming communities of coastal Karnataka (the Tulu Nadu region — Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts). (कंबाला — कर्नाटक)

 

• It is typically held between November and March, after the paddy harvest, and is closely associated with Tulu culture.

 

• Pairs of buffaloes, controlled by a runner, race through slushy tracks, and the event has both traditional and modern competitive formats.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable folk/traditional sporting festivals of India include Jallikattu (bull-taming, Tamil Nadu) and Bailgada Sharyat (bullock cart racing, Maharashtra).

 

NOTE

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 1): Known for festivals like Kullu Dussehra, not Kambala.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 2): Known for camel festivals such as the Pushkar Fair, not Kambala.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 4): Not associated with the Kambala festival.

question: Where does the Bay of Bengal Monsoon Branch and Arabian Sea Branch merge?
option_3: North Western Part of Ganga Plains
solution_text:
The correct answer is North Western Part of Ganga Plains.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The southwest monsoon splits into two branches over the Indian peninsula — the Bay of Bengal Branch and the Arabian Sea Branch. (मानसून की दो शाखाएं — गंगा के मैदान में मिलन)

 

• The Bay of Bengal Branch moves northward, strikes the Meghalaya hills and turns westward along the Himalayan foothills, while the Arabian Sea Branch moves northward over peninsular India and up the Indo-Gangetic plains.

 

• Both branches converge/merge over the north-western part of the Ganga (Indo-Gangetic) Plains, roughly around Punjab and Haryana.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Arabian Sea Branch further splits into three parts on hitting the Western Ghats — one giving rain to the west coast, one striking the Chotanagpur plateau, and one moving along the Aravallis giving scanty rainfall to Rajasthan.

 

NOTE

 

• Southern Part of Peninsular (Option 1): This is where the monsoon first arrives (Kerala coast), not where the two branches merge.

 

• Coromandel Coast (Option 2): This region receives rainfall mainly from the retreating/north-east monsoon, not the meeting point of the two branches.

 

• North of Deccan Plateau (Option 4): Not the actual convergence zone; the branches meet further north, over the Ganga plains.

question: Khelo India Winter Games started in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2020.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Khelo India Winter Games were first held in 2020, with the inaugural edition organised in Leh, Ladakh (22-25 January 2020), showcasing winter sports like ice hockey, skiing and skating. (खेलो इंडिया विंटर गेम्स — 2020)

 

• It is organised under the Khelo India scheme of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, aimed at promoting winter-sports talent from the Himalayan/high-altitude regions.

 

• Subsequent editions have been held across venues in Jammu & Kashmir (Gulmarg) and Ladakh (Leh).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The broader Khelo India Scheme (launched 2018) also encompasses the Khelo India Youth Games and the Khelo India University Games.

 

NOTE

 

• 2022, 2019, 2018 (Options 1, 3 & 4): None of these correspond to the year of the first Khelo India Winter Games; the inaugural edition was held in 2020.

question: Giddha and Bhagra are the folk dances of which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Giddha (a women's dance) and Bhangra (traditionally a men's harvest dance) are iconic folk dances of Punjab, performed especially during the Baisakhi harvest festival. (गिद्धा और भांगड़ा — पंजाब)

 

• Bhangra is energetic, performed to the beat of the dhol, and is associated with the wheat harvest season.

 

• Giddha is characterised by rhythmic clapping and traditional couplets called bolis.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Punjab's other cultural elements include the Gatka martial art and folk instruments like the tumbi and dhol.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat (Option 2): Known for Garba and Dandiya Raas, not Giddha/Bhangra.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 3): Known for dances like Chhau and Jhumair.

 

• Bihar (Option 4): Known for dances like Jat-Jatin and Kajari, not Giddha/Bhangra.

question: Which element's atomic number in the periodic table is named seaborgium, according to the notation of IUPAC nomenclature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 106.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Seaborgium (Sg) has the atomic number 106 in the modern periodic table, and is a synthetic, radioactive transactinide element. (सीबोर्गियम — परमाणु क्रमांक 106)

 

• It was named in honour of the American chemist Glenn T. Seaborg, a key figure in the discovery of several transuranium elements.

 

• It belongs to Group 6 of the periodic table, in the same group as chromium, molybdenum and tungsten.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Seaborgium was first synthesised in 1974; it is one of the very few elements to have been named after a living person at the time of naming.

 

NOTE

 

• 110 (Option 1): This is the atomic number of Darmstadtium (Ds).

 

• 102 (Option 3): This is the atomic number of Nobelium (No).

 

• 113 (Option 4): This is the atomic number of Nihonium (Nh).

question: Under the National Waterways Act, 2016, how many inland waterways have been declared as 'national waterways'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 111.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the National Waterways Act, 2016, a total of 111 inland waterways across India have been declared as National Waterways (NWs). (राष्ट्रीय जलमार्ग अधिनियम 2016 — 111 जलमार्ग)

 

• This Act merged the earlier five National Waterways (each declared by a separate Act) with 106 new waterways, bringing the total to 111, and repealed the previous individual Acts.

 

• National Waterway 1 (NW-1), on the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system (Prayagraj (Allahabad) to Haldia), is the longest national waterway.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National Waterways are developed and maintained by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), headquartered in Noida, under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

 

NOTE

 

• 109, 121, 132 (Options 2, 3 & 4): None of these match the actual figure of 111 national waterways declared under the 2016 Act.

question: A football match lasts two equal periods of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 45 minutes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Laws of the Game (framed by IFAB/FIFA), a standard football (soccer) match consists of two equal halves of 45 minutes each, totalling 90 minutes of regulation play. (फुटबॉल मैच — दो अर्ध, प्रत्येक 45 मिनट)

 

• A break of not more than 15 minutes (half-time) is allowed between the two halves.

 

• The referee may add injury/stoppage time at the end of each half to compensate for time lost.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• In a knockout match ending level, extra time of two 15-minute halves may be played, followed by a penalty shoot-out if the scores are still tied.

 

NOTE

 

• 40 minutes, 50 minutes, 20 minutes (Options 1, 2 & 3): None of these correspond to the actual duration of a standard football half, which is 45 minutes.

question: Ricky Kej won his third Grammy under which of the following categories?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Best Immersive Audio Album.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indian composer Ricky Kej won his third Grammy Award at the 65th Annual Grammy Awards (February 2023) in the Best Immersive Audio Album category, for the album 'Divine Tides' (with Stewart Copeland, Robert Väisänen and engineer Eric Schilling). (रिकी केज — तीसरा ग्रैमी, सर्वश्रेष्ठ इमर्सिव ऑडियो एल्बम)

 

• His first Grammy was in 2015 for 'Winds of Samsara' (Best New Age Album).

 

• His second Grammy was in 2022, also for 'Divine Tides', in the Best New Age Album category; the same album then won him a third Grammy in the newly introduced Best Immersive Audio Album category in 2023.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ricky Kej is a Bengaluru-based composer and environmentalist, also known for his work promoting sustainability through music.

 

NOTE

 

• Song of the Year, Album of the Year (Options 1 & 4): These are major general-field Grammy categories; Kej has not won a Grammy in either of these categories.

 

• Best Contemporary Instrumental Album (Option 2): This is a genuine Grammy category, but it is not the one in which Ricky Kej's third Grammy was awarded.

question: Who among the following was the most famous Shaka ruler, who got the Sudarshana Lake in Kathiawar renovated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rudradaman I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rudradaman I was the most celebrated ruler of the Western Kshatrapas (Saka/Shaka dynasty), who ruled in the 2nd century CE over Malwa, Gujarat, and Kathiawar. (रुद्रदामन प्रथम — सुदर्शन झील का जीर्णोद्धार)

 

• He is famous for repairing/renovating the Sudarshana Lake (originally built under the Mauryas) near Girinagar in Kathiawar, as recorded in the Junagadh Rock Inscription (150 CE).

 

• The Junagadh Rock Inscription is also historically significant as the first-ever long inscription in chaste/classical Sanskrit in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rudradaman I is also credited with defeating the Satavahana king (twice) but sparing his life due to a matrimonial relationship between the two dynasties.

 

NOTE

 

• Maues (Option 2): An Indo-Scythian (Saka) ruler of the north-west, often regarded as the first Saka king in India, unrelated to the Sudarshana Lake renovation.

 

• Rudrasimha III (Option 3): The last ruler of the Western Kshatrapa dynasty, defeated by the Gupta ruler Chandragupta II.

 

• Chashtana (Option 4): Founder of the Western Kshatrapa (Saka) dynasty at Ujjain, grandfather of Rudradaman I, but not credited with the lake renovation.

question: Agriculture sector is a part of the:
solution_text:
The correct answer is primary sector.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The primary sector of an economy includes activities that involve the direct extraction/use of natural resources, such as agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining. (प्राथमिक क्षेत्र — कृषि)

 

• Agriculture is the classic example of the primary sector, as it directly produces raw materials from land and nature.

 

• Sectors of an economy are generally classified as: primary (extraction), secondary (manufacturing), tertiary (services), and quaternary (knowledge-based services).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• In India, the share of agriculture in GDP has declined over the decades even as the sector continues to employ a large share of the workforce — a phenomenon linked to structural transformation of the economy.

 

NOTE

 

• Tertiary sector (Option 1): Comprises services such as banking, trade, transport and tourism, not raw material extraction.

 

• Secondary sector (Option 2): Comprises manufacturing and industry, which process raw materials into finished goods.

 

• Quaternary sector (Option 4): Comprises knowledge-based activities like IT, research and consultancy.

question: If the interest rate goes up, the demand for money will ___.
solution_text:
The correct answer is fall.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Keynesian theory of liquidity preference, the demand for money (especially speculative demand) is inversely related to the interest rate. (मुद्रा की मांग — ब्याज दर से विपरीत संबंध)

 

• When the interest rate rises, the opportunity cost of holding money (instead of interest-bearing assets/bonds) increases, so people prefer to hold less money and more interest-bearing assets, causing the demand for money to fall.

 

• Conversely, when interest rates fall, holding money becomes relatively less costly, so demand for money rises.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three motives for holding money under Keynes's theory are the transaction motive, precautionary motive, and speculative motive; the speculative motive is the one most sensitive to interest-rate changes.

 

NOTE

 

• First rise and then falls, rise, remain the same (Options 1, 2 & 3): None of these correctly describes the standard inverse relationship between the interest rate and money demand.

question: Which of the following states are a part of Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar and Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan was launched by the Prime Minister on 20 June 2020 from Khagaria, Bihar, as a 125-day employment and livelihood-generation campaign for migrant workers returning to villages after the COVID-19 lockdown. (गरीब कल्याण रोजगार अभियान — बिहार सहित 6 राज्य)

 

• It covered 116 districts across 6 states — Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Odisha, and Jharkhand — the states from which the largest numbers of migrant workers had returned.

 

• Both Bihar and Madhya Pradesh were among these six states, making Option 2 correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The scheme covered works across 25 categories, including rural housing, roads, and water conservation, spanning 12 ministries/departments.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat (Option 1): Gujarat was not one of the six states covered.

 

• Haryana and Bihar (Option 3): Haryana was not one of the six states covered.

 

• Assam and West Bengal (Option 4): Neither state was covered under this Abhiyaan.

question: Who was given the title of 'Hanjaba' by the Maharaj of Manipur for reviving Manipuri dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bipin Singh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Bipin Singh was a legendary Manipuri dance exponent, credited with reviving, refining and popularising Manipuri classical dance across India and internationally in the 20th century. (हंजाबा उपाधि — बिपिन सिंह)

 

• In recognition of his contribution, the Maharaja of Manipur conferred on him the title 'Hanjaba'; he also received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1966.

 

• He founded the Manipuri Nartanalaya to train and promote Manipuri dance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bipin Singh's disciples, including the Jhaveri sisters (Nayana, Suverna, Ranjana and Darshana Jhaveri), played a key role in spreading Manipuri dance further.

 

NOTE

 

• Charu Malhar (Option 1): Not associated with the Hanjaba title for Manipuri dance.

 

• Darshana Jhaveri (Option 2): A noted disciple of Guru Bipin Singh and a celebrated Manipuri dancer in her own right, but it was her guru, Bipin Singh, who received the Hanjaba title.

 

• Kalavati Devi (Option 4): Not the recipient of the Hanjaba title.

question: Which player among the following is the twenty-third Woman Grandmaster of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Priyanka Nutakki.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Priyanka Nutakki, a chess player from Andhra Pradesh, became India's 23rd Woman Grandmaster (WGM) after securing her final WGM norm at the 47th National Women's Chess Championship. (प्रियंका नुटक्की — भारत की 23वीं महिला ग्रैंडमास्टर)

 

• She achieved this feat as a teenager, also winning the National Junior Girls Chess Championship in the same period.

 

• The Woman Grandmaster (WGM) title is awarded by FIDE, the international chess federation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's first Woman Grandmaster was Subbaraman Vijayalakshmi, and India's first (full/open) Grandmaster was Viswanathan Anand.

 

NOTE

 

• Eesha Karavade, Bhakti Kulkarni (Options 2 & 3): Both are accomplished Indian Woman Grandmasters, but neither is the 23rd to earn the title.

 

• Subbaraman Vijayalakshmi (Option 4): She was India's first Woman Grandmaster, not the 23rd.

question: Creaming fat and sugar, whipping egg whites, or whipping heavy cream are examples of what type of leavening?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mechanical leavening.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mechanical leavening refers to the incorporation of air into a batter/dough through physical/mechanical action, such as creaming fat and sugar, whipping egg whites, or whipping heavy cream. (यांत्रिक खमीरीकरण — हवा मिलाना)

 

• The trapped air expands on heating (baking), causing the product to rise, without relying on a biological or chemical raising agent.

 

• Common baking techniques that use mechanical leavening include creaming, whipping, folding and sifting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Biological leavening uses living organisms like yeast, while chemical leavening uses agents like baking powder/baking soda that release carbon dioxide.

 

NOTE

 

• Organic leavening (Option 1): Not a standard recognised category of leavening in baking science.

 

• Physical leavening (Option 2): A near-synonym sometimes used loosely, but the precise, standard term for this air-incorporation method in baking classification is 'mechanical leavening'.

 

• Chemical leavening (Option 4): Relies on chemical reactions (e.g., baking soda plus an acid) to release CO₂ gas, not on physically whipping/creaming air into the mixture.

question: Who among the following signed the Poona pact with Mahatma Gandhi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhimrao Ambedkar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Poona Pact was signed on 24 September 1932 at Yerwada Central Jail, Pune, between Dr. B.R. Ambedkar (representing the depressed classes) and Mahatma Gandhi. (पूना पैक्ट — डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर)

 

• It followed Gandhi's fast unto death against the Communal Award (1932), which had proposed separate electorates for the depressed classes.

 

• The pact instead provided for reserved seats for the depressed classes within the general electorate, replacing the idea of separate electorates.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Poona Pact increased the number of reserved seats for the depressed classes in provincial legislatures compared to the Communal Award.

 

NOTE

 

• Ali Brothers (Option 1): (Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali) were leaders of the Khilafat Movement, not signatories of the Poona Pact.

 

• Chittaranjan Das (Option 2): A prominent Congress leader and founder of the Swaraj Party, not associated with the Poona Pact.

 

• Jyotiba Phule (Option 3): A 19th-century social reformer who predated the Poona Pact (he died in 1890) and was not a signatory.

question: Identify an organism that has a well-defined muscular pharynx.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ascaris.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ascaris is a parasitic roundworm (phylum Nematoda) that possesses a well-developed, muscular pharynx, which acts as a pump to suck in the host's partly digested food. (एस्केरिस — पेशीय ग्रसनी)

 

• The pharynx in Ascaris is a triradiate, muscular structure that aids in the ingestion and movement of food into the intestine.

 

• Ascaris is a common intestinal parasite in humans, causing the disease ascariasis.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nematodes like Ascaris show triploblastic, pseudocoelomate, bilaterally symmetrical body organisation.

 

NOTE

 

• Adamsia (Option 2): A sea anemone (Cnidaria), which has a simple gastrovascular cavity, not a muscular pharynx of this kind.

 

• Ctenoplana (Option 3): A member of phylum Ctenophora, lacking a well-defined muscular pharynx.

 

• Gorgonia (Option 4): Commonly known as sea fan, a colonial cnidarian, also lacking a well-defined muscular pharynx.

question: The concept of fundamental rights first came into being in the Magna Carta in __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is England.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The concept of fundamental/basic rights is traced back to the Magna Carta, signed in England in 1215 by King John, under pressure from rebel barons. (मैग्नाकार्टा — इंग्लैंड, 1215)

 

• The Magna Carta limited the powers of the monarch and established the principle that everyone, including the king, is subject to the law, laying an early foundation for civil liberties.

 

• It influenced later rights documents, including the English Bill of Rights (1689), and eventually the fundamental rights provisions of modern constitutions, including India's.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• In the Indian Constitution, Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III (Articles 12-35), inspired partly by the US Bill of Rights as well as this older English tradition.

 

NOTE

 

• The US (Option 2): Adopted its own Bill of Rights in 1791, which was influenced by, but came centuries after, the Magna Carta.

 

• Canada, Australia (Options 3 & 4): Neither is the origin of the Magna Carta; both are Commonwealth nations whose legal traditions were influenced by English common law.

question: The partially molten upper mantle material called __________ is a mechanically vulnerable layer beneath the lithosphere characterised by low seismic wave velocity and high attenuation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is asthenosphere.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The asthenosphere is the partially molten, mechanically weak layer of the upper mantle, lying just beneath the rigid lithosphere. (एस्थेनोस्फीयर — दुर्बलतामंडल)

 

• It is characterised by low seismic wave velocity and high attenuation (energy absorption) due to its semi-molten, plastic/ductile nature.

 

• The tectonic plates of the lithosphere are thought to 'float' and move over the asthenosphere, which enables plate-tectonic movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The asthenosphere extends from roughly 100 km to about 350 km below the surface, within the upper mantle.

 

NOTE

 

• Magnetosphere (Option 2): The region around Earth dominated by its magnetic field, unrelated to the mantle.

 

• Mesosphere (Option 3): In geology, refers to the lower mantle (below the asthenosphere); in atmospheric science, it names an atmospheric layer — neither matches this description.

 

• Stratosphere (Option 4): An atmospheric layer, not a layer of the Earth's interior.

question: Which player among the following won double gold at the 4th Para Badminton National Championship in December 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitesh Kumar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nitesh Kumar won a double gold at the 4th Para-Badminton National Championship, held in December 2021 in Odisha. (नितेश कुमार — दोहरा स्वर्ण, चतुर्थ पैरा-बैडमिंटन राष्ट्रीय चैंपियनशिप)

 

• He is a prominent Indian para-badminton player competing in the SL3 category (standing, lower-limb impairment).

 

• Nitesh Kumar went on to become a Paralympic gold medallist, winning gold in the men's singles SL3 category at the Paris 2024 Paralympics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has emerged as a strong force in para-badminton, with other notable players including Pramod Bhagat (Tokyo 2020 Paralympic gold medallist) and Manoj Sarkar.

 

NOTE

 

• Manoj Sarkar (Option 2): A decorated Indian para-badminton player (SL3), but not the double-gold winner at this particular championship.

 

• Pramod Bhagat (Option 3): India's leading para-badminton star and Tokyo 2020 Paralympic gold medallist, but not the double-gold winner at the 4th National Championship in December 2021.

 

• Tarun Dhillon (Option 4): An Indian para-badminton player, but not the athlete who won double gold at this event.
